set.q: A DNA profile from a crime scene would match about 1 in every million people. Police search a DNA database that holds profiles for only some of the city’s 5 million residents and find one match, a man with no other link to the crime. Which is best supported?

why: If the database covered the whole city, finding only one match would contradict 'about five people would be expected to match' and make option 3 arguable; the database must cover only part of the city.
Both tests (choosing a small risk over a far larger one) can also be read as ignoring the scale of harm, i.e. scope insensitivity.

set.why: Every other word names an angry verbal attack; a panegyric is a speech or piece of writing full of praise. Broadside may look unrelated, but it also means a fierce spoken or written attack.

why: 'Harangue may sound gentler' is an odd, unsupported claim; name the genuinely tempting distractor instead.

tests.s: Asked about the missing report, Kai says he already sent it, that his laptop crashed before he could finish it, and that nobody ever assigned it to him.
A teenager tells his parents he didn’t take the car, that he only drove it around the block, and that they had said he could use it anyway.

why: Original excuses ('already sent it', 'not due until next week') are consistent with each other, so the test did not clearly show mutually contradictory excuses.
